cards.headline: Born from fear of losing DJ coolness
cards.snippet: James Murphy, who wrote "Losing My Edge" (LCD Soundsystem's debut single, released in July 2002 on DFA Records), said it grew out of his time as a DJ. Playing records by Can, Liquid Liquid and ESG, he became cool for a moment, which he saw as a total anomaly. When he heard other DJs playing similar music, he worried that this newfound coolness would disappear. That fear is where the song comes from.
cards.context: Murphy explaining the song's inspiration in an interview.

cards.headline: The beat is a Killing Joke rip-off
cards.snippet: The rhythm of LCD Soundsystem's "Losing My Edge" is similar to "Change" by Killing Joke. Tim Goldsworthy, who co-founded DFA Records with James Murphy, admitted that the track was a rip-off of a Killing Joke track.
cards.context: Goldsworthy co-founded DFA Records with Murphy.

cards.headline: Two hours searching for the wrong band
cards.snippet: I heard this song on the radio, and then looked for "The Talking Heads - Losing My Edge" for like two solid hours.
cards.context: The song name-drops so many acts that a casual listener might guess it's a Talking Heads song, which it isn't.

replies.author: @postpunkfunk82
replies.text: Yup, they are heavily influenced by Talking Heads, especially the percussion section. One of the reasons I enjoy the hell out of LCD.

cards.headline: The cruelest, nicest line
cards.snippet: "I'm losing my edge, To better looking people... with better ideas... and more talent... and who are actually really really nice..."    Absolute Class.
cards.context: The punchline that the usurpers are better and nice is the song's sharpest self-own.

replies.author: @mrjohnnydangerously
replies.text: I was there. He's talking about me.

replies.author: @adampagria2510
replies.text: I hate it when they're nice.

cards.headline: Gardening to a hipster anthem
cards.snippet: I always sing "I'm pruning my hedge" to this when I do the garden.
cards.context: A pun on the title that turns an indie anthem into yard work.

replies.author: @sandrin0
replies.text: someone should get a hold of weird al and tell him about this

replies.author: @PhillipRemaker

cards.headline: Record store owners have heard it all
cards.snippet: As a former CD store owner, I swear that every line of this song has been uttered to me at some point.
cards.context: A commenter who ran a CD store says the song's snobbery matches customers he knew.

cards.headline: LCD Soundsystem open the encore at Alexandra Palace, 2017
cards.snippet: Recorded at Alexandra Palace in London on 22 September 2017, where the band used this as the start of their encore, running about eight minutes. One listener: "I love the uncertainty and jam session feel you get when LCDSS play live."
